doc.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Barnet as leader
summary: Barnet's generosity and his reputation as the white Ellington.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: How was Barnet as a leader? [ ? ? ] generous?

Barnet was a sweetheart, the greatest leader in the world. Every holiday or so – at one point, a holiday, he was giving the guys like Buicks and Chevrolets, Cadillacs, and stuff like that. But by the time I got with the band, he was giving a fifth of whiskey to every person.

I thought it was a great band, fantastic band. He was – Charlie was sometimes referred to as the caucasian Duke Ellington, and in many ways he was. He could have been compared to Ellington. He was a great musician, a fun-loving guy, a real down-to­ earth for-real person.
I’m trying to think now. I’m getting a little bogged down right now.
